messages:
rachel: FYI I'm opening a tiny docs PR: a compact 'cheatsheet' for customers migrating their tier mappings + short SDK snippets and analytics examples. Need a quick sanity-check on headers, export shape, and the onboarding panel link.

dev-docs: Drop the snippets here so I can verify header names and example payloads.

rachel: Pasting a minimal Python + curl pair we plan to include. Python (requests):

rachel: ```py
# per_request_tier.py
import requests
resp = requests.post(
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',
  json={'model':'redwood-13b','input':'Summarize the update'},
  headers={
    'Authorization':'Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY',
    'X-Redwood-Tier':'team-premium',  # prefer this tier (case-insensitive)
    'X-Redwood-Fallback':'cost-optimized'
  }
)
print(resp.json())
```

rachel: And a curl one-liner: 

rachel: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tier: team-premium" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Fallback: cost-optimized" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"Summarize the update"}'
```

thomas: LGTM. Two quick asks: (1) include a tiny analytics export example with the new field name `usage_tier`, and (2) call out how legacy burst credits surface (so BI teams know what to expect).

rachel: Adding analytics sample (JSON):

rachel: ```json
{"export": [
  {"meter":"tokens","usage_tier":"team-premium","count":15700},
  {"meter":"requests","usage_tier":"team-premium","count":210},
  {"meter":"burst_credits","usage_tier":"legacy-grant","count":35}
]}
```

thomas: Perfect. Also document that legacy burst credits appear in the quota API as a transient object named `graceAllowance` and as `legacy-grant` rows in exports. Add the CLI dry-run example so customers can safely preview consolidation.

rachel: Adding CLI: `redwood-cli quotas migrate --org $ORG_ID --dry-run` and the templated console link PM asked for: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboard/quota_migration_cheatsheet?org={{org_id}} (requires console:quota-read).

billing-bot: FYI billing schema change on 2026-01-05: field rename `tier_label` -> `usage_tier`. Docs should mention this to avoid confusion when customers compare historical exports.

dev-docs: Small editorial: avoid the word "slab" in new docs; use "legacy-grant" or "legacy-slab" only in historical notes. Also mention that some SDKs accept underscores in header names (e.g., `X_Redwood_Tier`).

rachel: Noted. I'll replace casual phrasing and add a short troubleshooting bullet: if a customer sees `tier_label` in exports, they likely have an old billing schema; ask them to contact finance with a sample export.

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5230  reviewers: @dev-docs @thomas

rachel: Thanks all. I'll squash the commits after CI and ping when merged. :thumbsup:
